==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Ulid&min=Ulid&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/UlidTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Ulid&min=Ulid&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
// Verify.Ulid: Scrubs ULIDs, both typed Ulid members and the 26 character form embedded in strings.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Ulid
// Note: Typed Ulid members go through a converter; ULIDs inside strings are found by a 26
// character window that has to sit on word boundaries and parse as a valid ULID, so false
// positives are unlikely.
// Note: The numbering is shared between the typed and the inline form, so one value reads the same
// everywhere in a snapshot.
// Note: There is no "verify a ULID" entry point: the value here is that no test has to opt in.
// Note: Verify.NUlid scrubs the same values and defines the same DontScrubUlids, so referencing
// both fails to compile (retired by C6).
// Note: The Ulid type is in the System namespace, so no using is needed.
public class UlidTests
{
    // A new ULID every run would fail every snapshot. Both the typed member and the copy inside
    // the string become Ulid_1, and the same value keeps the same number in both places.
    // Nothing is called per test: referencing the package is the whole opt-in.
    [Fact]
    public Task UlidScrubbing()
    {
        var id = Ulid.NewUlid();
        var customer = new Customer
        {
            Id = id,
            Name = "Sarah",
            Description = $"Sarah ({id})"
        };

        return Verify(customer);
    }

    // Stands in for a type of your own that carries a ULID. Nested here rather than in the
    // class library, so the library needs no reference to the Ulid package.
    class Customer
    {
        public Ulid Id { get; set; }
        public string Name { get; set; } = null!;
        public string Description { get; set; } = null!;
    }
}
